decision_reason: A1 provides useful broad motion contrasts, but jumping would benefit from an independent distinction based on repeated vertical body oscillation, transferable from running and stair activities. The nearly identical lying prototypes also lack a physically meaningful orientation distinction. Retain the remaining concepts: elevator motion is not reliably observable during constant-velocity travel, and class names alone do not establish stable additional distinctions between stepper and cross-trainer exercise or between sitting and standing. The supplied coverage and separation diagnostics motivate these checks but do not establish sensor-level predictability.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: vertical_oscillation_prominence
attributes.definition: Prominence of repeated gravity-aligned upward and downward torso motion relative to other torso motion, excluding monotonic transport.

levels.Low: Repeated vertical torso oscillation is absent or minor.
levels.Medium: Repeated vertical torso oscillation is appreciable but does not dominate torso motion.
levels.High: Repeated vertical torso oscillation dominates torso motion.

attributes.name: torso_lateral_inclination
attributes.definition: Degree to which the torso's anatomical left-right axis aligns with gravity, distinguishing lateral reclining from upright or face-up reclining configurations.

levels.Low: The torso's left-right axis is nearly perpendicular to gravity.
levels.Medium: The torso's left-right axis is oblique to gravity.
levels.High: The torso's left-right axis is nearly parallel to gravity.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports overall acceleration and rotation magnitude across the available body locations. Preserve the broad transfer from stationary and vigorous seen activities; effort and execution speed make adjacent levels ambiguous, especially for stepper versus cross-trainer exercise.
seen_anchors: running on a treadmill with a speed of 8 km/h

operations.reason: cadence: G6 supports repetition rate in limb acceleration and rotation. Walking and cyclic exercise provide transferable periodic patterns; short windows, irregular steps and ambiguity between steps and full cycles limit precision. Preserve rate rather than introduce an overlapping limb-specific cadence.
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

operations.reason: smoothness: G9 supports sustained rapid changes in acceleration, distinguishing continuous cyclic exercise from repeatedly abrupt motion. Transfer is available from cycling and running; vibration and execution style can blur levels. Static lying orientations do not justify different smoothness by themselves.
seen_anchors: cycling on an exercise bike in vertical positions
running on a treadmill with a speed of 8 km/h

operations.reason: impulsiveness: G10 supports brief abrupt changes associated with landing and foot contact. Descending stairs and basketball offer transferable impact examples for jumping. Landing technique and isolated elevator acceleration transitions introduce ambiguity; an elevator window need not contain a detectable transition.

posture_inclination: G1 supports gravity-relative orientation across torso and leg sensors. Standing, reclining and cycling provide posture anchors for sitting. Upright sitting can share torso orientation with standing, and unspecified leg-sensor placement limits certainty about seated geometry; retain the concept without claiming guaranteed separation.
seen_anchors: cycling on an exercise bike in horizontal positions

operations.reason: posture_variability: G12 supports changes in gravity-relative body configuration. Rowing and basketball supply transfer anchors for changing versus stable posture. Limb articulation alone does not establish global postural change, and moving around inside an elevator need not involve substantial torso inclination.

rotational_motion: G2 supports angular motion from torso and limb gyroscopes. Cyclic exercise and locomotion provide seen support for cross-trainer exercise and elevator movement. Turning is not guaranteed by moving around, while different limb rotations can yield similar overall rotational prominence.
seen_anchors: cycling on an exercise bike in vertical positions

operations.reason: translational_motion: G13 supports short-window translational-motion proxies, providing limited transfer from stair locomotion to parking-lot walking. These proxies cannot establish absolute displacement or reliably distinguish constant-velocity elevator transport from rest. Preserve the concept without adding an elevator-transport detector or treating treadmill motion as equivalent to environmental progression.

motion_regularity: G11 supports recurrence and predictability in multibody motion. Treadmill walking and basketball anchor structured and variable activity patterns for the close elevator-movement versus parking-lot-walking pair. Parking-lot walking may be steady and elevator movement may contain regular steps, so this is not a guaranteed separator.
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

operations.reason: vertical_oscillation_prominence: G1, G6 and G14 support gravity-referenced, repeated vertical torso acceleration relative to other directions. This adds directional structure beyond overall intensity and impact, supporting jumping versus walking or elevator movement through running and stair anchors. It does not require reconstructed jump height or inferred flight. Small jumps, stair-related torso bobbing and windows containing too few cycles can blur levels; elevator start-stop acceleration alone is not repeated self-generated oscillation.
seen_anchors: running on a treadmill with a speed of 8 km/h

operations.reason: torso_lateral_inclination: G1 supports the gravity-relative direction of the torso accelerometer under consistent anatomical mounting. It supplies an independent, physically justified contrast between the nearly identical lying prototypes rather than relying on their A1 smoothness difference. Upright sitting and standing provide a transferable low-lateral-inclination reference. Mounting misalignment, partial rolling and dynamic acceleration create ambiguity; this attribute does not distinguish sitting from standing.

semantic_redundancy_review: The 11 attributes retain distinct physical meanings. Cadence measures repetition rate, whereas motion_regularity measures predictability. Smoothness describes sustained rapid fluctuation, whereas impulsiveness describes brief peaks. Vertical_oscillation_prominence describes directional repeated torso motion rather than its total magnitude, impact strength or sustained progression. Torso_lateral_inclination describes lateral orientation, whereas posture_inclination describes overall upright-to-horizontal configuration and posture_variability describes change over time. Correlations are expected but do not make these concepts identical. No unsupported handle-use, thigh-specific, flight-phase, absolute-height or elevator-velocity attribute is introduced. Every A1 input and A2 output is accounted for once; no class-level vectors or empirical improvement claims are supplied.
